title: Deterministic Context Drift Gate Report
description: Read-only report emitted by the composed drift gate. Distinct from the refresh manifest (which records a durable operation) and from a branch-local context checkpoint (which is per-work-package): a gate report is transient, repository-wide, and exists to explain a build outcome. Its four result groups are disjoint, which is what lets a caller distinguish blocking drift from pending state and from external degradation -- a distinction the terminal refresh outcome collapses into a single degraded value.

schema_version.description: Contract version. Incremented only on a breaking change.

source_revision.description: Full Git SHA the gate evaluated. Every drift decision is made against this revision and producer inputs, never against file modification times.

outcome.description: Derived from the four result groups. 'fresh' covers the case where only informational drift or absent optional owners are present -- neither blocks.

exit_code.description: 0 fresh, 2 blocking drift, 1 apparatus failure or unverifiable provenance. Redundant with outcome, and emitted anyway so a log reader never has to re-derive the mapping.

blocking_drift.description: Producers whose committed managed output is stale. Non-empty implies exit_code 2 unless a failure outranks it. Sorted by producer_id for byte stability.

informational_drift.description: Producers whose drift reflects pending state rather than staleness -- currently only the OpenSpec projection producer, whose findings mean an active change carries an unmerged spec delta. Never contributes to a failing exit code.

not_configured.description: Optional owners that are absent. A required producer reporting no configuration is rewritten to a failure by registry policy before reaching here, so every entry is external degradation and none of them block.

failed.description: Producers that raised or could not render. Non-empty implies exit_code 1.

architecture.description: Architecture freshness determined by comparing committed provenance against recomputed digests. Never derived from rebuilding provenance out of the working tree.

freshness.description: 'unverifiable' covers missing, malformed, or schema-invalid provenance and is classified as blocking drift -- unverifiable evidence is not the same as absent tooling. 'not-configured' means the architecture owner is not importable and does not block.

provenance.description: State of the committed provenance file itself, reported separately so 'stale' and 'no baseline at all' are never confused.

context_impact.description: Work-package context-impact validation, scoped to work-package files present in the diff under test. Strict legacy enforcement is never enabled.

evaluated.description: Repository-relative paths of the work-package files validated. Empty when the diff touched none.

findings.description: Per-package outcomes. 'unmigrated' is reported explicitly and never fails the gate.

tree.description: Identity of the tree the verdict applies to (issue #385). A verdict is only comparable across environments when both graded the same tree; this block is what lets a reader see that a green local run and a red CI run graded different content instead of concluding the gate is nondeterministic. Optional for backward compatibility with schema_version 1 reports written before it existed; current gates always emit it.

head.description: Full SHA of the graded HEAD. Redundant with source_revision today, recorded separately so the tree block stays self-contained.

dirty.description: True when the working tree differs from HEAD, including untracked files -- producers render from the live filesystem, so untracked content is part of the graded tree.

base.description: The --base ref the changed-files diff was computed against.

base_upstream.description: origin/<base> when that ref exists locally, else null. Resolved read-only: no fetch, so the comparison is only as current as the last fetch.

commits_behind_base_upstream.description: Commits on base_upstream not reachable from HEAD. Non-zero means a run at the upstream tip grades different content. Null when base_upstream is null.

commits_ahead_of_base_upstream.description: Commits on HEAD not reachable from base_upstream. Null when base_upstream is null.

base_resolved_revision.description: The single revision the base name resolved to, and the revision every comparison in this run used. Recorded because a base NAME can resolve to more than one revision: `origin/<base>` and a local `<base>` branch diverge whenever the local ref is behind, and a report that silently compared against both describes no single tree.

base_resolved_from.description: Which ref supplied base_resolved_revision. 'remote' is preferred and is what a fresh CI checkout effectively uses; 'local' is the documented fallback for a checkout with no remote-tracking ref.

semantic.description: The gate never constructs an indexer and never probes Postgres or an embedder.

status.description: Deliberately not a SemanticIndexStatus value. Those describe probe outcomes; 'not-configured' would assert a probe found no configuration. 'not-attempted' makes no currency claim, so stale semantic results can never be presented as current.

reason.description: Why no probe was performed. Bounded like every other reason string in this contract family.

owner.description: Canonical owner, recovered from the registry producer spec. ProducerResult carries no owner field, so the gate joins the two.

artifacts.description: Every stale artifact named individually and sorted, so a failing build reports a precise list rather than a count.

attribution.description: Whether this finding was already present at the merge base ('inherited') or is attributable to the branch under test ('introduced'). 'indeterminate' is recorded when ownership cannot be decided from the available evidence, and is treated as inherited: falsely blaming a branch for the integration branch's debt is the failure this attribution exists to prevent, so the bias runs away from blame.

attributed_owner.description: Who is responsible for clearing this finding: the branch, or the integration branch.
